Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR ADJUSTABLE RANGE THERMOMETERS
0. 0.1This Indian FOREWORD

1

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 27 October 1977, after the draft finalized by the Laboratory Glassware and Related Apparatus Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Adjustable range thermometers can be used over a wide range of temperatures in several industrial, agricultural and scientific applications where the variations around a ` datum temperature' do not exceed a span of 6'C, and where precise measurement of variations in temperature is involved. Such thermometers can be used with advantage in studies of chemical micro-reactions, combustion phenomena, fuel evaluation, Use of germination of seeds, storage of cereals, micro-calorimetry, etc. such a thermometer, however, isnot recommended for measuring actual temperatures unless it is set with the help of a calibrated precision thermometer. 0.3 As adjustable range thermometers require to be first set at a datum temperature, a method for their proper setting and use, is described in Appendix A. 0.4 In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international coordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries, in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. This has been met by deriving assistance from IS0 4788-' Enclosed-scale adjustable-range thermometers ' issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). ,0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( ruviscd ).

1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements type adjustable range thermometers for measuring up to 6"C, in the range -20�C to +150X.

2. TERMINOLOGY 2.1 For the purpose of this standard the definitions 1%3*, in addition to the following, shall apply. given in IS : 2627the main scale

temperature at which 2.1.1 Setting Temperature -The of the adjustable range thermometer reads zero. 2.1.2 Setting - The process of adjusting meter to the required temperature range; setting temperature (see Appendix A ). the adjustable in other words,

2.1.3 Adjusting Device - That portion of the adjustable range thermometer which can be made to act as a reservoir of thermometric liquid which becomes surplus at the setting temperature. It enables the adjustment of the thermometer to read the setting temperature. 2.1.4 Temperature Span - The total maximum changes of temperature on either side of the ` datum temperature' for which the thermometer is to be used. This is given directly by the range of the main scale in degrees Celsius. 2.1.5 Immersion Level - In the adjustable range thermometers, position where the saddle ( seeFig. 1 ) is fused to the sheath. 3. 6.3.3 The bore of the capillary shall be wide enough to ensure that the jumping of the liquid meniscus without tapping does not exceed one half of the smallest division of main scale when observed by.unaided eye, while the temperature is rising at a uniform rate of O*l."C per minute or less. 6.3.4 Adjusting Device - The top of the capillary shall be provided an arrangement ( see Fig. 1 ) called the adjusting device. with

NOTE - In Fig. 1, Pattern A the adjusting device consists of a large bore U-tube joined to the capillary at one end and sealed at the other. In Fig. 1, Pattern B it consists of a truncated cylindrical gland through the bottom of which a capillary projects, ending in a jet. The other end of this gland is closed by fusing. *Specifkation for glass tubes for general purpose and reference thermometers.

IS : 8728 - 1977 6.3.5 The capillary and the adjusting device assembly shall be evacuated above the mercury column to such an extent that no difficulty is experienced in rejoining the mercury column during setting. 6.3.6 The volume of mercury contained in the capillary immersion level to the nearest graduation line on the main scale not exceed the equivalent of 2�C. from shall

6.4 Saddle - A suitable saddle shall be provided inside the sheath to support the main scale strip calm capillary assembly. It is a good practice to fuse the saddle to the sheath at the immersion level. 6.5 Scale Strip - The scale strip shall be placed firmly against the capillary tube, inside the sheath and shall be securely fastened at the top of the thermometer.
NOTE - A suitable method of fixing the scale strip is to fuse a glass tube or rod between the sheath and the top rnd of the scale strip, keeping the lower end free to slide in the saddle. Alternatively, the scale strip shall be fixed inside the sheath in any other suitable manner which permits differential expansion.

6.6 Scales - The thermometer shall have two scales as foIlows, shall be engraved or otherwise marked on the scale strip ( see Fig.

Auxiliary Scale - for approximate indication of the datum temperature between -20�C to +15O"C with graduation interval of 5�C.

6.7 Top Finish - The top end of the sheath shall be closed in a suitable manner and may be provided with a cap of some light metal or plastics which can stand continuous use of the thermometer at 150�C. 6.7.1 The cap may carry a hook or a ring for hanging the thermometer.

6.8 Calibration - The thermometer shall be graduated and calibrated for use in a vertical position, immersed up to the immersion level ( set Fig. 1 ) assuming the emergent column at the standard ambient temperature, that is, 27 f 2�C.

APPENDIX (Czausc 0.3 )
METHODS OF SETTING AND USE OF THERMOMETERS

A
ADJUSTABLE RANGE

A-O. GENERAL A-0.1 The temperature range of an adjustable adjusted by changing the volume of thermometric
capillary adjusting portion. This device ( seeFig. is done 1 ). by transferring namely, range thermometer is liquid.in the bulb and a part of it to the Pattern A and Pattern with

A-O.2 Two patterns of adjusting devices, B are in general use ( see Fig. 1 ).

A-O.3 Methods of adjusting ( or setting ) and use of thermometers each of these patterns of adjusting devices are given below. A-1.

ADJUSTABLE ADJUSTING

RANGE ~THERMOMETERS DEVICE OF PATTERN A
Bath See IS : 6274-1971*.

WITH

A-l.1 Apparatus A-1.1.1 Comparator
A-1.1.2 Reference setting temperature A-1.2 liquid

Thermometer -of the required ( see IS : 482.51968f ).

range

to

cover

the

- Heat the comparator bath filled with a suitable to the desired setting temperature and immerse the adjustable range thermometer in it. See whether the thermometer being set reads temperature higher or lower than the comparator bath temperature. Take the thermometer out of the bath, drain the liquid on the outside of the thermometer, wipe and then tilt to drain the mercury towards the bulb or towards the adjusting device, as necessary. After some mercllry has been transferred to the required side again insert the thermometer in the bath. Repeat the process till the thermometer begins to show almost `zero' on the main scale. It is now ready for exact adjustment.
A-1.2.1 Comjutation of Setting Temperature - Again put the thermometer being set in the bath, and allow it to acquire constant reading. Take the readings of this thermometer and the reference thermometer, apply to reference thermometer reading and compute the corrections temperature of the adjustable range thermometer for zero-reading on its main scale. This is the actual temperature to which the thermometer has been `set'.
*Method of ~calibrating liquid-in-glass thermometers. tSpecificationfor laboratory and reference thermometers.

Procedure

10

IS : 8728 - 1977 A-l.3 Use - In order to measure a temperature near about its setting temperature place the thermometer so `set' in the medium whose temperature is to be measured and note reading on its main scale. The actual temperature of the medium is then the algebraic sum of the set temperature and the reading of the main scale of the thermometer. A-1.3.1 In order to measure temperature difference between two media put the thermometer so set first in one medium, read its main scale and then put it in the second medium and again take the main scale reading. The difference between the two readings on the main scale is the requisite temperature difference between the two media. A-1.3.1.1 For such measurements, hotter medium first. it is often desirable to measure the

can also be precisely

studied

A-2.

ADJUSTABLE ADJUSTING

RANGE DEVICE

THERMOMETERS OF PATTERN B

WITH

A-2.0 General - The adjustment/setting is done by transferring a part of the mercury from the bulb to the gland or vice-versa. Skill is needed in transferring the mercury back into the capillary through the jet. This has to be done by carefully tilting the thermometer as the jet is a little~awav from the sides of the gland. Once the droplets of mercury enter the jet, they easily slide~down the capillary towards the bulb under gravity. A-2.1
jet

Apparatus

-

same as given in A-1.1.

A-2.2 Procedure - Transfer the whole mercury in the gland into the by skilful manipulation. Set t~he bath as in A-1.2. Insert the thermometer into the bath. Some mercury should flow into the gland; if it does not, it indicates that the bulb does not have sufficient mercury. Again transfer some mercury as above and again put the thermometer in the bath. Take the thermometer out of the bath when mercury stops flowing out of the jet. Cool the thermometer and repeat the process till mercury just stops flowing Out.
A-2.2.1 Fine Adjustment - The operation given in A-2.2 is repeated till the flow of mercury into the gland just stops after becoming extremely slow. The thermometer is now set for use,
